The reviewer cannot confirm Amaurose as a full-credit answer; a student would be credited for calling a small blind spot amaurose.

findings.issue: Indices 45, 47, 48, 49 contain the word “secreção”, which is both an everyday Portuguese word and the printed label of the keyed term, so the term stage is answered by the utterance itself. The subgroup stage still discriminates (Secreção is also a label under APARELHO AUDITIVO and MAMAS), and the eye is named in every utterance. findings.issue: A apostila não define Acuidade visual; imprime apenas a pergunta “Preservada ou não?” (p.1). O MeSH (D014792) descreve Visual Acuity como “Clarity or sharpness of OCULAR VISION or the ability of the eye to see fine details” e a expressa por medida (20/20). As falas são autorrelato de nitidez preservada em tarefas do dia a dia: não equivalem a medida de acuidade, não informam cada olho em separado e, salvo no índice 53, não dizem se há correção óptica.
findings.resolution: Accept source-based recognition of the function as “preservada” by self-report. No acuity value, eye-by-eye status or uncorrected acuity is established. Index 53 reports acuity with the usual glasses.

findings.issue: The ten Acuidade visual stories are normal-function reports. The reviewer compared each with Turvação visual, Escotomas, Diplopia, Amaurose, Fotofobia and Xantopsia (same subgroup), Acuidade auditiva, and the reading/writing entries Dislexia, Disgrafia and Afasias. findings.resolution: Reviewer agrees with the single accepted path in the ten items. A teaching reviewer may want to confirm that normal-function utterances are wanted for this entry, as the inventory's eligibility note states.

findings.issue: The batch maps two boundaries in one direction only. (a) The Epífora stories (indices 80–89) accept ocular Secreção as a second full-credit path, while Secreção stories that describe transparent or watery fluid (indices 47 and 49 here) accept Secreção alone. (b) All ten Escotomas stories (indices 60–69; 65–69 are out of scope) accept Amaurose but not Acuidade visual, while the Amaurose stories (indices 100–109) accept Acuidade visual: if a localized gap counted as Amaurose, the batch would still need to say why the Acuidade visual path that follows Amaurose elsewhere does not follow it here. findings.resolution: Recorded for the batch owner; the out-of-scope stories were read only to understand the mapping and are not judged here. The same teaching decisions settle both the held items of this report and their out-of-scope neighbours.

findings.issue: The batch references mesh-scotoma, mesh-blindness and mesh-visual-acuity-next01 give Portuguese paraphrases of the MeSH scope notes. The records read in this review agree with them in substance: Scotoma “A localized defect in the visual field bordered by an area of normal vision”; Blindness “The inability to see or the loss or absence of perception of visual stimuli”, with Amaurosis as a concept of that descriptor; Visual Acuity “Clarity or sharpness of OCULAR VISION or the ability of the eye to see fine details”. findings.resolution: Paraphrases are acceptable as locators. The use of mesh-blindness as support for the Amaurose path of the Escotomas stories is part of blocking finding B010-03.

unresolved.question: For “Depois de passar algumas horas fora, encontrei secreção transparente acumulada no canto dos olhos.”, is Secreção the only correct answer, or should Epífora also receive full credit? If Secreção alone is intended, should the utterance give an aspect that is not that of tears?

For “Notei uma secreção aquosa saindo do canto do olho esquerdo; a quantidade é pequena, mas se repete.”, should Epífora also receive full credit (as Secreção does in the Epífora stories), or should the utterance be rewritten with a non-watery aspect?

Should Amaurose (“perda total ou parcial da visão…”) receive full credit for an utterance that describes only a small localized gap with the rest of the scene seen normally? If yes, indices 60–64 can be released as keyed, and the course should also say whether Acuidade visual then follows, as it does in the Amaurose stories. If no, Amaurose must be removed from the accepted answers of all ten Escotomas stories and the items re-reviewed.

Where does the course draw the line between ocular Secreção and Epífora when the patient reports clear, transparent or watery fluid at the eye, and is “excesso de lágrimas mais que o normal” a requirement for Epífora or a gloss of “lacrimejamento”? The source line for Secreção is only an instruction (“anotar aspecto e quantidade”), and the external sources read here do not settle it.
